plan.title: Gradient descent: learning rate 0.1 vs 1.5 on the same bowl
plan.description: A stretched bowl-shaped loss surface has two balls starting from the same point. The blue ball uses learning rate 0.1 and the orange ball uses 1.5. With each step, both balls move against the slope (the gradient) and leave a trail. The blue ball creeps steadily toward the bottom. The orange ball overshoots, flips from side to side across the steep direction with bigger and bigger jumps, and soon leaves the surface (it diverges). Readouts show each ball's step count, loss and status.
plan.reason: Two balls run side by side on one surface from the same start, so you can compare them directly. Any difference you see comes only from the learning rate. You can also try rates in between to find where descent stops working.
interactions: Play or pause the host's steps to watch both balls move at once. Each step is one gradient descent update for each ball.
Take a single step for both balls to look at one update closely.
Change either learning rate. Both runs restart from the start point with trails cleared. Try a rate between 1 and 2: the ball settles along x but blows up along y.
Move the start point to see that the difference between the rates holds from other starting places.
Restart both runs from the start point, keeping your current settings.
assumptions: This is an illustration: a made-up bowl formula, not the loss of a real trained model.
The surface is loss = ½(x² + 2y²). It curves twice as steeply in the y direction as in the x direction.
Each step is exact gradient descent: new position = old position − learning rate × gradient. There is no noise and no momentum.

A ball settles in a direction only if the rate is below 2 ÷ that direction's steepness: below 2 along x, below 1 along y. At 0.1 both shrink each step (×0.9, ×0.8). At 1.5, x flips sign and halves each step while y flips and doubles, so the ball diverges.
A ball that leaves the drawn square (x and y from −3 to 3) stops there and is marked "diverged". At most 60 steps are run, so a very slow rate may still be short of the bottom when the run ends.
Heights are scaled down in the picture so the whole bowl fits in view. The loss readouts show the true values.
limitations: Real loss surfaces have many dimensions and are bumpy. This bowl only shows the basic effect of step size: too small is slow, too large overshoots or diverges.
With 1.5 at the default start, the orange ball leaves the surface after only two or three steps. Its trail is short on purpose, because that is what divergence looks like.
plan.learningGoal: See how the learning rate decides whether gradient descent creeps toward the minimum, zig-zags in, or overshoots and diverges, and that the safe rate depends on how steep the surface is.

findings.message: The plan promises a status readout for each ball, and a ball that leaves the square is supposed to be marked "diverged". The program computes statusA and statusB, but the readout bar shows only the losses and step counts, so no capture shows a status. Show the status somewhere the learner can see it, for example in each ball's tag text (e.g. 'lr 1.50 · diverged'), or as a readout the host displays

At the default start both balls sit at exactly the same point and size, so the orange ball completely covers the blue one. In the first view the learner sees one orange ball with two labels, and the blue (lr 0.10) ball is hidden. Make the start visibly shared without hiding blue: for example a small marker at the start, a slightly smaller or ringed second ball, or a tiny draw offset.

The default rate pair (0.1 vs 1.5) was only seen at step 0. The run at 0.1 was not sampled; 0.14 was sampled instead. The program's update x(1−r), y(1−2r) is correct, so blue at 0.1 should converge before the 60-step limit.

Orange has diverged (trace statusB='diverged', loss 16.1953 checks out: the ball reached (0.625, 4) after 2 steps). No readout or label shows this, and the ball is drawn clamped at the edge, so the learner cannot tell it diverged rather than stopped. The status readouts are missing from view.
The 'lr 0.14' tag, the blue ball, the minimum dot and the 'Minimum' label crowd together near the centre.
Both balls diverged (losses 84.125 and 16.1953 are correct for rates 2 and 1.5), but no status is visible. Both balls just look parked at the edge.

In the default view the 'lr 1.50' tag sits at the start point beside the blue trail, about 150 px from the orange ball, which is unlabelled at the left. It reads as labelling the wrong object. Keep each tag next to its ball (change its placement or offset).
Same as v0-s0: the status readouts the plan promises are not shown.
The orange ball is clamped at the edge, but nothing shown says 'diverged'. The status readout is missing.
Each long trail segment appears as a thick line with a separate thin line beside it, a drawing artefact of the host's trail.
Both balls diverged, but no status is visible. The status readouts are missing.
The trail segments are drawn doubled (thick plus thin line).
